EVS brings computer vision to automobile production lines, deployed at final inspection points to detect surface defects, verify assembly completeness, and flag anomalies before vehicles leave the line. Teams can reduce manual review while maintaining high quality standards.
The system captures detailed defect data — location, type, severity — and makes it available in real-time dashboards for production supervisors.

Production Planning

With clearer machine data from visual inspection, production planners can identify bottleneck stations, measure defect trends over time, and plan corrective actions with confidence. The result is better planning for every downstream process step.

name: Textile
metaTitle: Textile Fabric Inspection & Quality Reporting | Edraak Systems
metaDescription: Edraak's AI vision inspects 100% of fabric at production speed — 8x faster than manual checks — with meter-to-meter quality reports, roll grading, and automated label application.
intro: AI-powered vision inspection for fabric defects, meter-to-meter quality reporting, and automated label application — delivering 100% inline fabric inspection at 8x the speed of manual checks.
outcome: Outcome is 100% fabric inspection coverage, 8x faster defect detection, automated meter-to-meter quality reports, reduced rework and waste, and seamless label application integrated into the production line.
details: Edraak's vision systems inspect fabric for defects at full production speed, generate detailed meter-to-meter quality reports for clients, and automate label application. The process is eight times faster than manual inspection and guarantees 100% fabric inspection coverage, eliminating blind spots in quality control.
subtitle: AI Vision Inspection, Quality Reporting & Automated Labeling for Textiles

pageContent.text: 100% Inline Fabric Inspection at Production Speed

Edraak's vision inspection systems are installed directly on production lines to scan every meter of fabric at full line speed. Unlike traditional manual inspection — which typically samples only a fraction of production — EVS delivers 100% fabric inspection coverage, catching defects that human inspectors would miss due to fatigue, speed limitations, or visual constraints.

The system detects a comprehensive range of defects including holes, stains, weaving errors, color variations, selvedge defects, slubs, and contamination. Each defect is precisely mapped to its meter-level location on the fabric roll, enabling accurate downstream marking, grading, and removal.
8x Faster Than Manual Inspection

Manual fabric inspection is slow, inconsistent, and labor-intensive. EVS automates the entire visual inspection process, operating at speeds that are up to eight times faster than manual checking. Production lines maintain their throughput while achieving higher detection accuracy and complete coverage — every roll, every meter, every defect.

This speed advantage means textile manufacturers can inspect 100% of production without bottlenecking downstream processes, eliminating the need for separate offline inspection tables and reducing work-in-progress inventory.
Automated Meter-to-Meter Quality Reporting

EVS automatically generates detailed meter-to-meter quality reports for every fabric roll. These reports document defect type, location (by meter), size, severity, and frequency for the entire roll length. Reports can be shared directly with clients as part of quality assurance documentation, building trust and reducing disputes over fabric quality.

The reporting system provides roll-level grading based on defect density and severity, helping manufacturers sort fabric by quality tier. This enables tiered pricing, optimized cutting plans, and better inventory management.
Integrated Label Application

Beyond inspection, EVS integrates automated label application directly on the production line. Once fabric passes inspection, the system triggers label placement at precise locations — defect markers, roll identification, grade labels, and client-specific tagging. This eliminates a separate manual labeling step and ensures every roll is accurately identified before it leaves the production floor.
Real-Time Defect Mapping & Roll Grading

As fabric passes through the inspection zone, each defect is recorded with its exact meter position, type classification, and severity score. The system builds a complete defect map for every roll in real time, enabling immediate grading decisions. Rolls can be automatically classified as first-quality, seconds, or reprocess based on configurable threshold rules.

This real-time grading gives production teams instant visibility into fabric quality, allowing them to make informed decisions about rerouting, reprocessing, or releasing rolls without waiting for offline inspection results.
Reduced Waste, Rework & Manual Labor

By catching defects early in the production process, EVS prevents defective fabric from progressing to downstream operations where rework costs are higher. Early detection reduces material waste, minimizes rework, and lowers the labor cost associated with manual inspection headcount.

Manufacturers typically see a significant reduction in customer returns and quality complaints after implementing automated vision inspection, improving both operational efficiency and brand reputation.
Key Benefits

Up to 8x faster than manual inspection

name: Pharma
metaTitle: Pharma Blister Inspection & OEE Monitoring | Edraak Systems
metaDescription: Edraak's AI vision inspects pharmaceutical blister packs for broken, cracked, or missing pills, auto-rejects defects, and tracks OEE, efficiency, and downtime.
intro: Installed in blister scanning lines, the cameras identify defects such as broken or cracked pills, alert the system for automatic removal, and collect Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), machine efficiency, and downtime data.
outcome: Outcome is reliable blister pack QA, automatic rejection of defective items, real-time OEE collection, machine efficiency tracking, downtime analysis, and full batch-level traceability for regulatory compliance.
details: Edraak's vision systems are installed on pharmaceutical blister scanning lines where high-resolution cameras inspect every cavity for defects including broken or cracked pills, missing tablets, incorrect fill, and sealing issues. When defects are detected, the system automatically alerts rejection mechanisms to remove non-conforming packs. Beyond inspection, the technology continuously collects Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), machine efficiency, and downtime data — giving pharma manufacturers a complete quality + production monitoring solution.
subtitle: Blister Scanning, QA Inspection & OEE Data Collection for Pharmaceuticals

pageContent.text: High-Speed Blister Pack Cavity Inspection

EVS is installed directly on blister scanning lines, where high-resolution line-scan cameras inspect every individual cavity at full production speed. The system detects broken or cracked pills, missing tablets, incorrect fill levels, sealing defects, and foreign contamination — all without slowing the packaging line.

Each blister is analyzed cavity by cavity, ensuring that no defective product passes through to downstream packaging or dispatch. The system's advanced vision algorithms can distinguish between subtle variations in pill appearance, fill levels, and seal integrity that would be difficult or impossible to detect consistently with manual inspection.
Automatic Rejection of Defective Blisters

When a defect is identified, the system triggers an immediate alert to the line control system, which activates pneumatic or mechanical rejection mechanisms to remove the non-conforming blister from the production stream. This automated rejection happens in real time at line speed, ensuring that only compliant product continues downstream.
Rejection events are logged with timestamps, defect type, cavity position, and batch information, creating a complete audit trail for every removed blister.
Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) Data Collection

Beyond inspection, EVS continuously collects Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) data from the blister scanning line. The system tracks machine availability, performance efficiency, and quality rate — the three core OEE metrics — and presents them through integrated dashboards.

OEE data is collected automatically without requiring manual data entry. Production managers can view real-time OEE scores, identify performance bottlenecks, and track improvement initiatives over time.
Machine Efficiency & Downtime Tracking

EVS monitors machine operating states to calculate efficiency metrics and record every downtime event — whether planned (changeovers, maintenance) or unplanned (jams, breakdowns, material shortages). Each downtime event is tagged with duration, cause category, and timestamp.

Downtime reports highlight the most frequent and longest-duration stoppages, helping engineering teams prioritize root-cause analysis and continuous improvement efforts. By correlating downtime data with inspection results, manufacturers can identify whether quality issues are contributing to line stoppages and vice versa.
Real-Time Alerts & Production Visibility

When defect rates exceed configurable thresholds or when machine efficiency drops below target levels, EVS sends real-time alerts to operators, supervisors, and maintenance teams. This immediate visibility enables rapid response to quality or production issues before they escalate into larger problems.
Production dashboards display live line status, current OEE, defect counts, reject rates, and machine state — giving every shift team a single source of truth for line performance.
Batch-Level Traceable Reporting

All inspection results, rejection events, and OEE data are logged against specific batch numbers with timestamps, creating a complete digital record for every production run. Reports support internal quality audits, regulatory documentation, and customer compliance requirements.

Traceable reporting helps pharmaceutical manufacturers demonstrate GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) compliance, respond to regulatory inquiries with accurate data, and continuously improve both product quality and production efficiency.

Real-time alerts for defect rate and efficiency thresholds
